classification.difficultyReason: Interpret depression and motion parallel to the cliff, then distinguish horizontal yacht distance from observer-to-yacht distance. Link horizontal and vertical right triangles to obtain the new distance and depression angle.

content.prompt: From the top of a cliff that runs north–south, the angle of depression of a yacht, 200 metres out to sea and due east of the observer, is $20^\circ$. When the observer next looks at the yacht, he notices that it has sailed 150 metres parallel to the cliff.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the height of the cliff, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the cliff height in metres. The angle of elevation from the yacht equals the angle of depression.
$$\begin{align*}\tan20^\circ&=\frac{h}{200}\\h&=200\tan20^\circ\\h&\approx73\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
Keep $200\tan20^\circ$ unrounded for subsequent parts.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance the yacht is from the observer after it has sailed 150 metres parallel to the cliff, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.short:
$260\text{ m}$

Use Pythagoras’ theorem in the horizontal plane, then in the vertical triangle.
answer.worked:
The yacht's motion parallel to the cliff is perpendicular to its initial 200 m eastward displacement. Let $r$ be its new horizontal distance from the foot of the cliff and $d$ its distance from the observer, both in metres.
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=200^2+150^2\\r&=250.\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded cliff height,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=250^2+(200\tan20^\circ)^2\\d&=\sqrt{250^2+(200\tan20^\circ)^2}\\d&\approx260\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the angle of depression of the yacht from the top of the cliff when it is in its new position, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the new angle of depression. It equals the angle of elevation in the vertical right triangle with horizontal side 250 m.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{200\tan20^\circ}{250}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{200\tan20^\circ}{250}\right)\\\theta&\approx16^\circ.\end{align*}$$
